rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 30, Simplified Method: "You must use the Simplified Method if either of the following applies. 1. Your annuity starting date was after July 1, 1986, and you used this method last year to figure the taxable part. 2. Your annuity starting date was after November 18, 1996, and both of the following apply." The model says the hiding condition (retirement.annuity, condition 2) omits condition 1. Condition 1 alone reaches only an annuity starting from July 2, 1986 to November 18, 1996 (a later start that met the method last year met condition 2 on its starting date, which does not change); retirement.special refuses "a pension or annuity in which you have after-tax cost whose annuity starting date was before November 19, 1996, or for which the Simplified Method does not apply (the General Rule)" and is read by retirement.taxable, so every condition-1-only annuity is refused (screen retirement.special). The English of the line and of its condition is right for every entry the tool computes. Not raised by the model, and ruled separately: the same condition shows the worksheet on IRA entries (F5) and on annuities whose cost was recovered before 2025 (F6). Project stands on the English.

rulings.model: The gate limits the line to the second Simplified Method condition (annuity starting date after November 18, 1996, with the age/guaranteed-payment tests), but the IRS text says you must use the Simplified Method if either that condition or 'your annuity starting date was after July 1, 1986, and you used this method last year'; the restatement omits the latter condition.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 30, Simplified Method: "You must use the Simplified Method if either of the following applies. 1. Your annuity starting date was after July 1, 1986, and you used this method last year to figure the taxable part. 2. Your annuity starting date was after November 18, 1996, and both of the following apply." The model says the hiding condition (retirement.annuity, condition 2) omits condition 1. Condition 1 alone reaches only an annuity starting from July 2, 1986 to November 18, 1996 (a later start that met the method last year met condition 2 on its starting date, which does not change); retirement.special refuses "a pension or annuity in which you have after-tax cost whose annuity starting date was before November 19, 1996, or for which the Simplified Method does not apply (the General Rule)" and is read by retirement.taxable, so every condition-1-only annuity is refused (screen retirement.special). The English of the line and of its condition is right for every entry the tool computes. Not raised by the model, and ruled separately: the same condition shows the worksheet on IRA entries (F5) and on annuities whose cost was recovered before 2025 (F6). Project stands on the English.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 29, Simplified Method Worksheet, Table 1 for Line 3: "AND your annuity starting date was-- before November 19, 1996, enter on line 3... after November 18, 1996, enter on line 3... 300 360 260 310 240 260 170 210 120 160". The before-November-19-1996 column is screened: retirement.special refuses ("Form 1099-R special cases") a distribution involving "a pension or annuity in which you have after-tax cost whose annuity starting date was before November 19, 1996", and retirement.annuity, which routes to the worksheet, asks for "an annuity starting date after November 18, 1996". The refused set includes the p. 30 condition 1 annuities ("Your annuity starting date was after July 1, 1986, and you used this method last year") that start before November 19, 1996; that is a documented scope reduction, not a computation error. Same as the archived rulings, rechecked against the current rendering.
